_about: Published figures that pipeline/build_validation.py compares with this site's Comtrade figures. Each check gives the published value, its source and a measure the script computes from site/data/plastic_<year>.json (reported routes after cleaning; imputed and modelled years are never used). Sets: '*' all economies, 'EU27', 'OECD' (current members), '!X' everything outside X, 'MLIC' the World Bank's middle- and low-income groups in that year, or a list of Comtrade codes. 'share_of' turns the measure into a percentage of a second measure. 'rule': 'views' gives exporters' and importers' figures separately; 'larger' also gives the larger of the two reports route by route, used only where a study did that. 'years' with 'agg': 'mean' averages several years. 'stream' uses a waste that carries plastic amongst other materials instead of HS 3915. Values in tonnes unless unit is '%'. 1 lb = 0.45359237 kg.

findings.title: China's 2016 imports
findings.text: Comtrade had replaced China's 2016 import weight with its own estimate (8.80 Mt at US$420 a tonne), against the 7.35 Mt China reported. The site now takes each partner's reported weight for those routes, which gives 7.95 Mt. China's own figures for 2008 to 2015 are as reported.

findings.title: Hong Kong's 2013 exports
findings.status: Fixed: Hong Kong's usual price used.
findings.text: Comtrade's estimated weight for Hong Kong's 2013 exports was 1.49 Mt, against about 3 Mt in 2012 and 2014 at similar values. Partners' reports cannot stand in, because China books most of these shipments to the country of origin, so the site divides each value by Hong Kong's own US$ per tonne in 2012 and 2014. This gives 2.42 Mt.

findings.title: Hong Kong re-exports
findings.text: Until 2017 most waste shipped to Hong Kong went on to China and is counted twice in world totals, once into Hong Kong and once into China: 2.8 Mt in 2016 by Hong Kong's reports. The studies above count it the same way.

findings.title: Larger of the two reports
findings.text: Taking the larger report for each route gives world totals 20 to 30% above either side's total, because exporters and importers often book the same shipment to different partners. Any single resolved figure per route inherits part of this.

findings.title: Partners' reports for US and EU exports
findings.text: US and EU exporters' figures match US Census and Eurostat closely. Importers record more: Malaysia records three times what the US reports sending in 2023, and in 2022 Türkiye recorded a fifth more than the EU reported sending.

findings.title: Plastic in recovered paper
findings.text: The site assumes 2% plastic in recovered paper (HS 4707). IPEN (2023) uses 5 to 30% for paper bales.

findings.title: Basel Convention data
findings.status: Not usable as a volume check.
findings.text: OECD countries reported 17,193 t of plastic waste exports under the Basel prior informed consent procedure in 2021, against 5.21 Mt reported to Comtrade (OECD, 2024). Most plastic waste trade falls outside that procedure.
